text:
alex: quick q — seeing `401 invalid_scope` when streaming with a service-account token that impersonates different projects. root call works fine, but after the stream reconnect the sdk seems to reuse the wrong token. anyone run into this?
maria: yup, saw that last week. issue is the token cache key in the Node/Python clients didn’t include the requested project/audience pair, so refresh returns the global token and the server rejects it. log looks like: `oauth: token has no audience for project-abc -> 401`.
jonathan: is this only for impersonation flow or OIDC id_tokens too?
maria: both can be affected depending on how you request them. impersonation via `serviceAccounts.generateIdToken` vs OIDC `aud` param — both need the audience/project baked into the cache key.
sara: curious — does streaming reconnect flow trigger a refresh at all? I thought we only refresh on expiry.
maria: streaming client keeps a short-lived connection and will attempt to re-open on network blips. current client logic re-uses the cached token on reconnect; if reconnect happens in a different project context (multi-tenant apps) it fails.
alex: repro steps I used: create SA that can impersonate two projects, open a long stream scoped to project-A, then simulate reconnect and call with project-B header. server rejects.
jonathan: thanks — can you paste the header you send?
alex: header is `x-redwood-project: project-b` plus `Authorization: Bearer <id_token>`
maria: short-term hack: include the project in the auth metadata so the cache key becomes `<uid>:<aud>:<project>`. Example patch we used in staging:```js
// pseudo: token cache key
const cacheKey = `${serviceAccountEmail}|${requestedAudience}|${projectId}`;
```
jonathan: perfect, that explains it. will this affect Dedicated/private control planes?
maria: Dedicated/private control planes accept the same JWT/OIDC flows; SDK bug sits client-side so it affects any deployment mode where a single client instance talks to multiple projects.
sara: any language-specific quirks? we have a flaky python-only repro.
maria: Python client used a different cache layer (LRU without request-scoped keys). PR we drafted touches both runtimes. Node change is smaller. Python needs a small refactor to thread the project param into the cache key + tests.
jonathan: PR is up: github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/4523 — adds project to cache key and adds an integration test that spawns two streams and forces reconnects.
dev-bot: CI pipeline started for redwood/sdk#4523 (unit + integration)
alex: can reviewers pls check specifically streaming reconnect test — I added a flakey-safe retry. also note the patch adds a new opt on streaming: `stream({ project: 'project-b', reauth_on_reconnect: true })` — default false to avoid perf regressions.
sara: fyi product asked whether this change will require migration notes. answer: only SDK bump, no server changes.
maria: rollout plan: merge to main, canary to npm/pypi with tag `canary-multi-project`, monitor token error rate and stream failures for 24h. if green, cut patch 0.21.4 with changelog.
jonathan: gonna ping @eng-oncall to watch streaming error rate during canary window.
athan: (reacts :thumbsup:)
alex: thanks all — I've left a small debug helper in the PR to log `cacheKey` when `REDWOOD_DEBUG=auth` so we can trace repros.
maria: sounds good. if CI passes I'll merge this afternoon.
jonathan: leaving a review now.
sara: awesome, thanks — this should fix the python streaming flake we’ve been triaging.
alex: resolved for me locally, will test canary once published.
dev-bot: redwood/sdk#4523 merged to main by maria — canary artifacts published.
